title: docs(adr): ADR-0145 — ui `?: never` tombstones retire on the spec's one-major window

_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8JeHddgk25VvfwwsRzoP6xU)_

Fixes #25912

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：新增一篇 ADR-0145（根 `docs/adr/`）并重生成 ADR 索引：ui 授权面上的 `?: never` 墓碑按 spec 自己的窗口退场，退役后再保留一个 major，到 R+2 major 切出时到期，绝不更长；只立规则，不删任何墓碑、不改代码。
- 为什么改：执行本卡的维护者字母 A（裁决 6407810703）；ui 授权面只增不减，每个墓碑都成了永久义务。
- 风险与回滚：只有文档，无发布面；风险在规则措辞本身（容器豁免、R 的读法），回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：ADR 的 D1（规则）、D2（R 怎么读，含早于 ADR-0087 与只属 ui 的退役）、D3（删墓碑不能把拒绝变成静默接收）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm check:adr-index && pnpm check:adr-anchors && node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs`，应全部 exit 0。
- 需要你做的：Tier H，等契约复核 PASS 与席位 ACCEPT 后由您批准合并；在那之前本 PR 保持草稿。

## What changes

- **New record** `docs/adr/0145-ui-deprecation-tombstones-retire-on-the-spec-window.md` (Proposed; becomes Accepted by the maintainer's merge). It records letter A and states:
  - **D1, the rule.** A `?: never` tombstone leaves the ui authoring face in the first release after the spec major in which its ADR-0087 conversion expires: carried through protocol major R + 1, due from the cut of R + 2, the same cut at which ADR-0087's 2026-10-26 addendum removes the spec's kit. One clock (the protocol major, never the npm major). The window binds both ways: a ui tombstone neither leaves before nor outlives the spec kit for the same key.
  - **D2, reading R.** Spec-named retirements read R from the spec (`RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`, else the release-tag clock the spec's deletion gate uses). A retirement that predates ADR-0087 is counted as if its conversion had run the one-major window from the major it retired in, so no such tombstone gets a fresh window. A ui-only retirement runs the same window from the first `@object-ui/types` release that carried it. Undated means not due, never guessed.
  - **D3, the container carve-out.** A deletion must leave a refusal: the TS member stays while its container is open (an index signature); the zod twin stays where its container is `.passthrough()` or strips, which is ADR-0087's own strip-container rule and the posture `agedOutSpecKeyRefusal` already takes. Derived faces move together.
  - **D4, the changeset.** `minor` (never `major`), a **Breaking** note naming each `Type.key` and its remedy, plus the declaration lines and ADR-0087 disposition marker the gates require, not restated.
  - **Applying the rule.** How the first batch enumerates, dates (`git log -S` on a full clone; pre-merge ui history is in `objectstack-ai/objectui`, not here), judges and re-pins.
- **Regenerated index** `docs/adr/README.md` (`pnpm adr:index`).

## Why

Ruling 6407810703 (maintainer letter A, 2026-10-25T01:46Z) over seat options 6407810621. Not taken: B (remove when the spec retires the key) and C (no rule).

## Tests

None. This PR declares a rule and changes no code, so there is no behaviour to pin or ablate.

## Acceptance notes

- **Registry.** The record is in the root `docs/adr/`: #26080 ruling A keeps `ui/docs/adr/` as the frozen ObjectUI import (indexed under `ui-`, files untouched), and `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` resolves only the root registry, so a new ui decision lands here; Prime Directive #13 places an ADR in the repository whose code it governs. No written rule continues new ui decisions in `ui/docs/adr/`. Number 0145: open PR #27239 holds 0144, and no other open PR adds a root record at or above it (the file lists of all 20 open PRs, read through REST before numbering).
- **Premise readings** (`origin/main` `9dec0545`, `ui/packages/types/src`, tests excluded): 520 `@deprecated` tags and 675 `?: never` lines (the card read 574 and 640 on 2026-10-24 objectui). The card's "16 `z.never` tombstones" does not hold: the zod tombstones are now spelled through the helpers in `zod/tombstone.zod.ts` (`retirementTombstone`, `agedOutSpecKeyRefusal`, `aliasKeyRefusal`, `handlerKeyRefusal`, `retiredNodeType`), several hundred call sites, so the ADR names the zod twin by what it mirrors rather than by a count. Per ui/AGENTS.md #9 the ADR records no count; the instrument is in "Applying the rule".
- **Reading for the contract review.** The ruling's text keys the window to a spec retirement. Most ui tombstones name a ui-only retirement (an objectui card) with no spec key behind them. D2 runs the same window from the ui's own retirement release. This is the narrowest reading consistent with "the window the spec itself runs, never a longer one", and the review should confirm it.
- **D3 and the "two faces retire together" facet.** The ruling's facet ① has the zod and `.d.ts` faces retire together. D3 keeps that wherever a deletion leaves a refusal. Where the zod container is `.passthrough()` (everything derived from `BaseSchemaCore`), deleting the twin would make the tolerant face keep the key silently. That is the Prime Directive #12 defect ADR-0087's 2026-10-26 addendum refused for the spec's 58 strip-container tombstones, so the twin stays there until its container closes.
- **Not here.** The ui/AGENTS.md #0.1 pointer line rides #25919's AGENTS.md PR, as the ruling's item 3 says. No sweep: the first application batch is its own card after this merge.
- **Tier H.** `docs/adr/**` is the register row `adr` (`glob: 'docs/adr/**', tier: GOVERNED_TIER_H` in `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`). `dispatch-gates --tier` derives the mandatory ceiling model tier for `docs/adr/**`, with the effort floor at xhigh. This card ran at TIER_DEFAULT under the measured quota exemption the claim records ("ceiling tier unavailable, contract review handed to triage at review time"). Changed lines 160 (+157 / −3) against the 3,000 threshold: under.
- **How this PR was opened** (#26617: relay `pr_create` requests the governed approvers on a diff touching a governed path). `11b3e687` adds the record, `98dcc57e` reverts it so the PR opened with an empty net diff and no approver requested, and `01db9123` re-applies it, so the head's tree equals `11b3e687`'s. The seat requests approvers after the contract review PASS and its ACCEPT.
